name: Hookwires
location_notes: Wire extends to skin; easily found at pleural surface
limitations_and_risks: Bleeding (9–35%), pneumothorax (32–68%), pain, displacement; requires same-day surgery
best_for: Superficial nodules needing direct pleural localization

name: Microcoils
location_notes: Coiled wire inserted transecting lesion; pleural or contralateral side anchoring
advantages: Less pain than hookwires; high intraoperative localization (90–100%)
limitations_and_risks: Risk of embolization, pneumothorax, bleeding; occasional displacement
cautions: Occasional need for fluoroscopy if pleural visualization inadequate
post_procedure_care: CXR for ptx if symptomatic; proceed to OR

name: Methylene blue
location_notes: Percutaneous or bronchoscopic injection; aim to tattoo visceral pleura
advantages: Does not impact pathology; safe; inexpensive
limitations_and_risks: Narrow utility window (<3 hours); risk of pleural ‘spillage’

name: NIR/IR/ICG
advantages: Visible through 1–2 cm of tissue; slower diffusion; retains fluorescence ≥5 hours
limitations_and_risks: Same-day surgery still preferred; possible failure if too deep
best_for: Subpleural or buried lesions up to ~2 cm depth
cautions: Depth limits signal; coordinate NIR equipment

name: Barium
cautions: Place adjacent to avoid histologic artifact

name: Lipiodol
advantages: Remains in situ for months; inexpensive; no inflammatory artifact; compatible with cyanoacrylate

name: Radiotracer (technetium-99)
advantages: No intraop fluoroscopy required; high VATS localization (88–96%)
limitations_and_risks: Radiation handling/logistics; half-life ~6 hours; ptx risk 7–30% with CT delivery; rare pleural soiling
best_for: ORs with gamma detection; when fluoroscopy is undesirable
cautions: Radiation safety for all teams; schedule surgery same day
